sec: Allen's test and the ABG procedure · p826

items.q: Allen's test is performed to determine:
opts: Patency of the ulnar artery alone
Depth of the radial artery from the skin
items.exp: Allen's test: determines patency of radial artery (both ulnar and radial arteries are occluded with a clenched blanched palm). (Book p826)

items.q: Match the steps of the ABG procedure as printed — 1) Wrist position  2) Palpation  3) Sterilisation  4) Needle angle … A) 45°  B) Non-dominant hand extended by 20–30°  C) Radial artery palpated  D) Area sterilised
items.exp: Steps: wrist of the non-dominant hand extended by 20–30°, radial artery palpated, area sterilised, sample taken with the needle at 45°. (Book p826)

items.q: The needle is inserted at which angle for radial ABG sampling?
items.exp: The sample is taken with the needle at 45 degrees. (Book p826)

items.q: How far is the wrist extended for radial puncture?
items.exp: The wrist of the non-dominant hand is extended by 20–30°; the needle enters at 45°. (Book p826)

items.q: Match the figure labels of the Allen's test — 1) Clenched blanched palm  2) Radial artery  3) Ulnar artery … A) Occluded along with the radial artery in the figure  B) The arm whose patency is being tested  C) Sign of the hand posture used
items.exp: The figure labels the clenched blanched palm, the radial artery occluded, and the ulnar artery also occluded — the test determines patency of the radial artery. (Book p826)

items.q: Which artery is palpated with the index finger in the procedure figure?
items.exp: The procedural figure shows palpation of the radial artery with the index finger before the 45° puncture. (Book p826)

items.q: ‘The ABG procedure is performed on the dominant hand, with the wrist flexed, using a 45° needle angle.’
opts: False — it is the non-dominant hand with the wrist extended 20–30° and the needle at 45°
True — dominant hand, wrist flexed, needle at 45°
False — it is the non-dominant hand with the wrist extended 45° and the needle at 20–30°
True, except that the needle angle should be 90°
items.exp: The wrist of the non-dominant hand is extended by 20–30° and the sample is taken with the needle at 45°. (Book p826)

items.q: After the puncture, the sample is capped and transported. What does the figure show next?
opts: Sample discarded if blood is bright red
Needle left open to air to avoid bubbles
items.exp: The third panel of the procedure figure is labelled ‘Needle capped and transported’. (Book p826)

items.q: All but one of these are printed steps of the ABG procedure. Which is the odd one out?
opts: Local anaesthetic infiltration of the puncture site
items.exp: The printed steps are wrist extension by 20–30°, palpation of the radial artery, sterilisation of the area, and sampling with the needle at 45° — no local anaesthetic step is listed. (Book p826)
